rendered: The authors did not choose room temperature as the separation condition. The Cyrene-based separation was run at an elevated temperature: a Cyrene-based separation process at an elevated temperature[1], because the PVDF binder dissolves in Cyrene only at high temperature (DSC: the PVDF binder dissolved in Cyrene at ~90 °C[2]). Room temperature appears only in supporting roles. First, after the hot separation the supernatant is cooled to room temperature temperature to induce phase separation[3], so that PVDF precipitates and can be filtered off with the recycled solvent. Second, room-temperature filtration serves as a comparison. At room temperature PVDF precipitates and gels on cooling: started to precipitate out and gelation occurred[4]. This causes the PVDF to redeposit on the cathode material: the reprecipitation of PVDF along with the cathode particles after[5] cooling. The room-temperature runs therefore show the failure mode that the elevated-temperature separation is designed to avoid.
